title: Expense totals by category
brief: Every Friday the expense tool gives me expenses.csv and I spend an hour in a spreadsheet adding up each category. I want a small file, category_totals.csv, with one line per category and the biggest spend on top. My manager only reads the first lines.

skill.title: csv.DictReader and csv.writer
skill.card: csv.DictReader(f) gives each row as a dict keyed by the header, so row["amount"] is the amount column. Every value is a string: convert with float() before adding. csv.writer(f).writerow([...]) writes one line and handles quoting for you.
skill.example:
import csv
with open("demo.csv", "w") as f:
    w = csv.writer(f)
    w.writerow(["category", "amount"])
    w.writerow(["Meals", "12.50"])
with open("demo.csv") as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        print(row["category"], float(row["amount"]) * 2)

task: Read expenses.csv (columns date,employee,category,amount) and add up the amount of each category. Write category_totals.csv with the header category,total, then one row per category sorted by total, highest first, each total with 2 decimals (182.40). Finally print one line with the number of categories: ~~~text Categories: 4 ~~~
solution:
import csv

totals = {}
with open("expenses.csv") as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        totals[row["category"]] = totals.get(row["category"], 0) + float(row["amount"])

with open("category_totals.csv", "w") as f:
    w = csv.writer(f)
    w.writerow(["category", "total"])
    for category, total in sorted(totals.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True):
        w.writerow([category, f"{total:.2f}"])

print("Categories:", len(totals))
hint: sorted(totals.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1], reverse=True) puts the biggest total first, and f"{total:.2f}" keeps 2 decimals.

skill.title: json.load and json.dump
skill.card: json.load(f) turns a JSON file into dicts and lists, and json.dump(data, f, indent=2) writes them back. JSON null becomes None, so test it with is None.

task: Read tickets.json. Its key tickets is a list of dicts with id, status (open or closed) and assignee (a name, or null). Print two lines, the ids in file order: ~~~text Open: 4 Unassigned: 102, 104 ~~~ Then write triage.json with indent=2 holding {"open": 4, "unassigned": [102, 104]} for that data.
starter:
import json

with open("tickets.json") as f:
    data = json.load(f)
solution:
import json

with open("tickets.json") as f:
    data = json.load(f)

open_tickets = [t for t in data["tickets"] if t["status"] == "open"]
unassigned = [t["id"] for t in open_tickets if t["assignee"] is None]

with open("triage.json", "w") as f:
    json.dump({"open": len(open_tickets), "unassigned": unassigned}, f, indent=2)

brief: Our web shop writes server.log all day. When customers phone to complain, I want to know at once which hours had errors and which error keeps coming back. Keep it short, I read it on my phone.

skill.title: Reading a log line by line
skill.card: Loop over the file one line at a time and cut each line with split(" ", 3): at most 3 cuts, so the message keeps its own spaces. collections.Counter counts anything, and most_common(1) gives the winner with its count.
skill.example:
from collections import Counter
line = "2025-03-07 09:02:44 ERROR Payment gateway timeout"
date, time, level, message = line.split(" ", 3)
print(time[:2], level, message)
c = Counter(["a", "b", "a"])
print(c.most_common(1))

task: Read server.log. Each line is date time LEVEL message; skip blank lines. For the ERROR lines only, print one line per hour that had errors, hours in order, then the most frequent error message: ~~~text 09h: 2 errors 10h: 1 errors 11h: 1 errors Top error: Payment gateway timeout (3 times) ~~~
starter:
from collections import Counter

by_hour = Counter()
messages = Counter()

with open("server.log") as f:
    for line in f:
        pass
solution:
from collections import Counter

by_hour = Counter()
messages = Counter()

with open("server.log") as f:
    for line in f:
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        date, time, level, message = line.strip().split(" ", 3)
        if level == "ERROR":
            by_hour[time[:2]] += 1
            messages[message] += 1

for hour in sorted(by_hour):
    print(f"{hour}h: {by_hour[hour]} errors")
message, count = messages.most_common(1)[0]
print(f"Top error: {message} ({count} times)")
hint: The hour is time[:2]. After the loop, messages.most_common(1)[0] is a (message, count) pair.

title: Name the scanned invoices
brief: Our scanner drops files like SCAN_07032025_Dupont.pdf into scans/. Nobody can sort them by date, and the client names are all over the place. I want 2025-03-07_dupont.pdf. Do not touch anything else in that folder, the scanner keeps its own notes there.

skill.title: os.listdir, os.path.splitext, os.rename
skill.card: os.listdir("scans") lists the names in a folder; wrap it in sorted() so the order is always the same. os.path.splitext(name) splits off the extension, and os.rename(old, new) renames a file. Build full paths with os.path.join.
skill.example:
import os
name = "SCAN_07032025_Garage Leroy.PDF"
stem, ext = os.path.splitext(name)
tag, d, client = stem.split("_", 2)
print(ext.lower(), d[4:], d[2:4], d[:2], client.lower().replace(" ", "-"))
print(os.path.join("scans", name))

task: For every file in scans/ whose name starts with SCAN_ and ends with .pdf (any case), rename SCAN_DDMMYYYY_Client Name.pdf to YYYY-MM-DD_client-name.pdf: client in lowercase, spaces replaced by -, extension .pdf. Leave other files alone. Go through the names in sorted() order, print each rename, then the count: ~~~text SCAN_01042025_martin.pdf -> 2025-04-01_martin.pdf SCAN_07032025_Dupont.pdf -> 2025-03-07_dupont.pdf SCAN_12032025_Garage Leroy.PDF -> 2025-03-12_garage-leroy.pdf Renamed: 3 ~~~
starter:
import os

renamed = 0
for name in sorted(os.listdir("scans")):
    print(name)
solution:
import os

renamed = 0
for name in sorted(os.listdir("scans")):
    stem, ext = os.path.splitext(name)
    if not stem.startswith("SCAN_") or ext.lower() != ".pdf":
        continue
    tag, d, client = stem.split("_", 2)
    new = f"{d[4:]}-{d[2:4]}-{d[:2]}_{client.lower().replace(' ', '-')}.pdf"
    os.rename(os.path.join("scans", name), os.path.join("scans", new))
    print(name, "->", new)
    renamed += 1
print("Renamed:", renamed)
hint: stem.split("_", 2) gives the tag, the date and the client (the client may contain spaces). d[4:] is the year, d[2:4] the month, d[:2] the day.

title: Payment reminder letters
brief: Every month I copy and paste the same reminder letter for each customer who has not paid. Names, amounts, dates: I always get one wrong. Here is my letter with blanks in template.txt and the late payers in overdue.csv. One file per invoice, please.

skill.title: string.Template fills the blanks
skill.card: Template(text) marks blanks with $name. substitute(row) fills them from a dict, so a csv.DictReader row works directly; extra columns are simply ignored. A missing key raises an error instead of sending a half filled letter.
skill.example:
from string import Template
t = Template("Dear $name, invoice $invoice is late.")
row = {"name": "Alice Moreau", "invoice": "INV-1042", "email": "a@b.fr"}
print(t.substitute(row))

task: Fill template.txt once per row of overdue.csv (columns name,email,invoice,amount,due) and write the result to reminders/<invoice>.txt, for example reminders/INV-1042.txt. Create the folder first with os.makedirs("reminders", exist_ok=True). Print one line per letter: ~~~text Wrote reminders/INV-1042.txt Wrote reminders/INV-1057.txt ~~~
starter:
import csv
import os
from string import Template

with open("template.txt") as f:
    template = Template(f.read())
solution:
import csv
import os
from string import Template

with open("template.txt") as f:
    template = Template(f.read())

os.makedirs("reminders", exist_ok=True)
with open("overdue.csv") as f:
    for row in csv.DictReader(f):
        path = f"reminders/{row['invoice']}.txt"
        with open(path, "w") as out:
            out.write(template.substitute(row))
        print("Wrote", path)

title: Load the stock into a database
brief: The warehouse system exports stock_export.csv every night. Our reporting team wants it in stock.db so they can query it, and I want a quick total per warehouse when the load is done. The table is already created, it is just empty.

skill.title: sqlite3: executemany with ? placeholders
skill.card: sqlite3.connect("stock.db") opens the database file. con.executemany(sql, rows) runs one INSERT per tuple, each ? filled in order. Call con.commit() to save, then loop over con.execute("SELECT ...") to read rows back as tuples.
skill.example:
import sqlite3
con = sqlite3.connect(":memory:")
con.execute("CREATE TABLE stock (sku TEXT, warehouse TEXT, qty INTEGER)")
con.executemany("INSERT INTO stock VALUES (?, ?, ?)", [("A1", "Lyon", 3), ("A1", "Lille", 5), ("B2", "Lyon", 2)])
con.commit()
for wh, total in con.execute("SELECT warehouse, SUM(qty) FROM stock GROUP BY warehouse ORDER BY warehouse"):
    print(wh, total)

task: Open stock.db as con. Its table is stock (sku TEXT, name TEXT, warehouse TEXT, qty INTEGER). Insert every row of stock_export.csv (same column names) with executemany and ? placeholders, qty as an int, and commit. Then, with one SQL query using GROUP BY warehouse ORDER BY warehouse, print: ~~~text Loaded 5 rows Lille: 25 Lyon: 134 Nantes: 86 ~~~
starter:
import csv
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect("stock.db")
solution:
import csv
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect("stock.db")
with open("stock_export.csv") as f:
    rows = [(r["sku"], r["name"], r["warehouse"], int(r["qty"])) for r in csv.DictReader(f)]
con.executemany("INSERT INTO stock VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", rows)
con.commit()

print("Loaded", len(rows), "rows")
for warehouse, total in con.execute("SELECT warehouse, SUM(qty) FROM stock GROUP BY warehouse ORDER BY warehouse"):
    print(f"{warehouse}: {total}")
hint: Build a list of tuples with a comprehension over csv.DictReader, then one con.executemany("INSERT INTO stock VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", rows).

brief: We have a handful of scheduled jobs and every Monday someone asks me when the next backup is. jobs.csv lists each job with its days and time. Give me a machine that takes the current date and time and tells me the next run of every job.

skill.title: datetime, timedelta and weekday()
skill.card: datetime.strptime(text, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") turns text into a datetime. replace(hour=2, minute=0) moves to a time of the same day, + timedelta(days=1) goes to the next day, and weekday() gives 0 for Monday up to 6 for Sunday.
skill.example:
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
DAYS = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]
now = datetime.strptime("2025-03-07 10:00", "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
t = now.replace(hour=2, minute=0) + timedelta(days=1)
print(DAYS[t.weekday()], t.strftime("%d/%m %H:%M"))

task: Read the current time from input(), like 2025-03-07 10:00. For each row of jobs.csv (columns name,days,time, days like Mon Tue Wed), find the first moment strictly after now that is at that time on one of those days. Print one line per job, in file order, with DAYS[t.weekday()] and t.strftime("%d/%m %H:%M"): ~~~text Backup: Sat 08/03 02:00 Stock export: Fri 07/03 18:30 Payroll check: Mon 10/03 09:00 Bin collection mail: Sun 09/03 20:00 ~~~ No sleeping and no real clock: only date maths.

solution:
import csv
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

DAYS = ["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]
now = datetime.strptime(input(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")

with open("jobs.csv") as f:
    for job in csv.DictReader(f):
        hour, minute = job["time"].split(":")
        t = now.replace(hour=int(hour), minute=int(minute))
        while t <= now or DAYS[t.weekday()] not in job["days"].split():
            t += timedelta(days=1)
        print(f"{job['name']}: {DAYS[t.weekday()]} {t.strftime('%d/%m %H:%M')}")
hint: Start at today with the job's time; while that moment is not after now, or its day is not in the job's days, add one day.

title: Skip discontinued items
brief: The warehouse system got an upgrade and the nightly export changed. The reporting team also complained that discontinued items inflate the totals. Please load only what we still sell.
task: stock_export.csv changed: - the column qty is now called on_hand, - a new last column status is active or discontinued. Insert only the active rows (the table stock does not change: on_hand goes into qty). Loaded N rows counts the inserted rows, and the totals per warehouse come from the table as before.
solution:
import csv
import sqlite3

con = sqlite3.connect("stock.db")
with open("stock_export.csv") as f:
    rows = [(r["sku"], r["name"], r["warehouse"], int(r["on_hand"])) for r in csv.DictReader(f) if r["status"] == "active"]
con.executemany("INSERT INTO stock VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", rows)
con.commit()

print("Loaded", len(rows), "rows")
for warehouse, total in con.execute("SELECT warehouse, SUM(qty) FROM stock GROUP BY warehouse ORDER BY warehouse"):
    print(f"{warehouse}: {total}")
hint: Add if r["status"] == "active" at the end of the comprehension, and read r["on_hand"].

client: Helene Marchand, CFO at Maison Marchand
title: The monthly sales pipeline
brief: Each shop's till drops one CSV per month into exports/, and they are a mess: shop names in any case, amounts that are not numbers, American dates, orders exported twice. Every quarter my team spends two days cleaning them by hand. I want them cleaned, loaded into reports.db, and one report.txt I can forward to the board.

skill.title: Extract, transform, load, report
skill.card: A pipeline reads every input (sorted(glob.glob("exports/sales_*.csv"))), cleans each row, and counts bad rows instead of crashing: wrap float() and datetime.strptime() in try/except ValueError. A set of seen ids catches duplicates. Load the good rows into SQL and let one query build the report.
skill.example:
from datetime import datetime
seen = set()
for oid, date, amount in [("A1", "2025-01-04", "12.5"), ("A2", "01/04/2025", "3"), ("A1", "2025-01-04", "12.5")]:
    try:
        datetime.strptime(date, "%Y-%m-%d")
        value = float(amount)
    except ValueError:
        print(oid, "rejected: bad value")
        continue
    if oid in seen:
        print(oid, "rejected: duplicate")
        continue
    seen.add(oid)
    print(oid, "kept", value)

task: Process every file matching exports/sales_*.csv, in sorted name order (other files are ignored). Columns: order_id,date,shop,amount. - Clean the shop: strip spaces and title case it ( lille becomes Lille). - Reject a row (count it in rejected) when the shop is empty, the amount is not a number, the date is not YYYY-MM-DD, or the order_id was already seen. - Insert the good rows into the table sales (order_id TEXT, date TEXT, shop TEXT, amount REAL) of reports.db (open it as con) and commit. - With one SQL query, total the amount per shop, highest first. - Write report.txt and print the same text: ~~~text Loaded 6 rows, rejected 4 Nantes: 345.00 Lille: 290.50 Lyon: 135.25 ~~~

    print(path)
solution:
import csv
import glob
import sqlite3
from datetime import datetime

rejected, good, seen = 0, [], set()

for path in sorted(glob.glob("exports/sales_*.csv")):
    with open(path) as f:
        for row in csv.DictReader(f):
            shop = row["shop"].strip().title()
            try:
                amount = float(row["amount"])
                datetime.strptime(row["date"], "%Y-%m-%d")
                if not shop or row["order_id"] in seen:
                    raise ValueError("empty shop or duplicate order")
            except ValueError:
                rejected += 1
                continue
            seen.add(row["order_id"])
            good.append((row["order_id"], row["date"], shop, amount))

con = sqlite3.connect("reports.db")
con.executemany("INSERT INTO sales VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)", good)
con.commit()

rows = con.execute("SELECT shop, SUM(amount) AS total FROM sales GROUP BY shop ORDER BY total DESC")
report = "\n".join([f"Loaded {len(good)} rows, rejected {rejected}"] + [f"{shop}: {total:.2f}" for shop, total in rows])
with open("report.txt", "w") as f:
    f.write(report + "\n")
print(report)
hint: Do the float() and strptime() checks inside one try; raise ValueError yourself for an empty shop or a seen order_id, so one except counts every bad row. ORDER BY total DESC in SQL gives the report order.
